result:
Each pair of distinct circles meets in at most 2 points, and there are C(4,2) = 6 pairs, so there are at most 12 intersection points. Twelve is attainable when every pair intersects in two points and no point is shared by three circles. Such a configuration exists, for example four circles of equal radius placed in general position with centers close together.

Solution A claims 14, which exceeds the upper bound. Its counting is also faulty. It has all circles pass through A and B, so those points are shared rather than new, and it then counts additional points beyond what the pairs allow.

Solution B's reasoning and answer of 12 are correct.

WINNER: B
